clue.text: Surface from which mistress catches a cold

indicators.note: the mistress catches, i.e. holds within her, the next pieces

parts.note: a madam is a mistress of a household or brothel
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone blames a hard surface for giving the lady of the house a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac-style road paving of crushed stone is a type of road surfacing.

clue.text: Sea sickness's second business for doctor

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: the second letter of the word sickness is taken

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: Someone works out which firm handles seasick patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Medico is informal for a medical practitioner.

clue.text: Brave ploy, extremely sinister

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, and the Cree are a Native American people

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, the first and last letters of ploy

explanation.surface: A bold scheme turns out to be very menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is the old term for a Native American warrior, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something creepy gives you the shivers, just as something ominous does.

clue.text: Doctor being fired for asking questions in the military

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A dismissed medic faces grilling from army officers.
explanation.definitionFit: After a mission, soldiers are questioned to gather what they learned.

clue.text: Underground ring supporting police officer in the end

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so the ring comes last

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: in the end means the final letter of officer

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A ring is held up beneath a police officer at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Metro is a name for underground railways such as the Paris Métro.
explanation.definitionFit: Metro is the name for a city subway railway, such as the one in Paris.

clue.text: Unpleasant type among workers, perhaps, is a scold

indicators.note: the unpleasant type sits among the workers, so it goes inside them

parts.note: worker bees are the example implied by 'perhaps'
a rat is slang for a nasty, treacherous person

explanation.surface: In an office, one nasty colleague among the staff turns out to be a nag.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase: someone who berates others is a scold, so 'is a scold' stands for the verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold is to tell off harshly, and one who keeps doing so behaves as a nagging critic.

clue.text: Top of the hill and round the corner to catch black animal of North America

parts.note: the brow is the top of a hill

indicators.note: near catches black, so it holds the black piece

parts.note: round the corner means nearby
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hunter tries to snare a dark beast near the crest of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The grizzly is a North American subspecies of this large bear.

clue.text: Some light, flat receptacles, defaced

indicators.note: defaced means losing the face, the first letter

parts.note: trays are flat containers for carrying things

explanation.surface: Light falls on some flat dishes that have been vandalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Beams of sunlight are a portion of light.

clue.text: 19's right old hat photo inside hat

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as "19's right old hat photo inside hat" (6,2,9): the blog's parse O + PIC + OF + CAP inside TRICORN needs 'of' and has no job for 'right', so the clue as held is garbled and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: 19's right old hat photo inside hat

clue.text: See 25
Nerd observing partners between the sheets, lying back

indicators.note: the partners go between the sheets, so they sit inside the bed word
lying back says the bed word is read from right to left

parts.note: being between the sheets means being in bed
West and East are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A geek spies on a couple in bed, an image the solver is meant to wince at.
explanation.walkthrough: Partners are West and East, as at bridge. 'observing' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a socially awkward, studious type, much as a nerd is: they are slang synonyms.

clue.text: Brace alongside square piece of wood

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of pheasants
by means beside, alongside
four is the square of two, a square number

explanation.surface: A carpenter fixes a support next to a square timber offcut.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of timber with a two-inch by four-inch cross-section is a standard building lumber size.

clue.text: See 7
Sibelius, perhaps, finding bit of fluff in navel

indicators.note: only a bit of the words fluff in navel is wanted, a run spanning them

explanation.surface: A composer is pictured picking lint out of his belly button.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sibelius' is the example: Jean Sibelius was Finnish. 'finding' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Sibelius was a native of Finland, so he is an example of a person from that country.

clue.text: Participant in rally unlikely to welcome British Olympic success, beginning to boo

indicators.note: the first word welcomes the rest, so it holds them inside

parts.note: tall as in a tall story, one hard to believe
Jessica Ennis won heptathlon gold for Britain at the London 2012 Olympics

indicators.note: beginning to boo means its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone unhappy with a British gold medal starts booing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rally' sounds political but is the to and fro of a tennis point. 'unlikely' is TALL as in a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball struck back and forth in a long rally takes part in every exchange.

clue.text: Present line of newspaper previews not for publication

indicators.note: of newspaper comes before, or previews, the present line, so those pieces come first

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
here means present, in attendance
a cord is a line or string

explanation.surface: A newspaper's teasers for a current story are said to be not yet printable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'previews' puts 'of newspaper' first though the clue gives it second; FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark made unofficially, which journalists agree not to print or attribute, is confidential.

clue.text: First-class, Stairway to Heaven, possibly?

definitions.meaning: first-class means of the highest rank
a stairway reaching heaven would be the highest set of stairs of all

explanation.surface: A great rock song is called first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stairway to Heaven' suggests the Led Zeppelin song, but it is read literally as a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: First-class means of the highest level, and the uppermost set of stairs is literally the highest one.

clue.text: See 17
19's demon fatal, as he's a phoney

indicators.note: phoney means fake, so the letters are falsified into a new order

explanation.surface: A deadly demon is unmasked as a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is MILLER: this is Arthur Miller's play. 'phoney' rearranges DEMON FATAL AS HES A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Miller wrote this 1949 play about Willy Loman, so it is Miller's.

clue.text: Spectacular drawers so?

definitions.meaning: those who inhale or draw in breath are inspiring, so drawers of awe are inspiring it

explanation.surface: Someone's underwear is pronounced magnificent, a joke on drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' looks like underwear but means people who draw in; to inspire is to breathe in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spectacular fills onlookers with wonder, and the second reading takes inspiring literally as drawing in wonder.

clue.text: Runner penning line for one in tale

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as sheep in a pen

parts.note: a miler is a runner over a mile

explanation.surface: An athlete writes a line for a character in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The Canterbury Tales include a tale told by one of the pilgrims, a corn grinder.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims include this flour grinder, who tells a bawdy tale.

clue.text: Dave's partner Lawrence, virgin

parts.note: Chas and Dave were a London singing duo
T. E. Lawrence was Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: A list of famous names ends with someone pure.
explanation.walkthrough: Chas and Dave were a British cockney rock duo; T. E. Lawrence is known as Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sexually inexperienced means being pure, abstaining.

clue.text: Food — ork, eef and hicken?

parts.note: the three words are pork, beef and chicken each with the first letter lopped off, so the word for food is a beheaded word for butcher's produce

explanation.surface: A diner reads out a menu with every dish's first letter missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork, beef and chicken have each lost their first letter; do the same to their collective name, M-less, and a word for food is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to consume food, and the noun for food is informal slang for grub.

clue.text: England cricketers Tony and Robin, the opener

parts.note: Tony Lock was an England spin bowler of the 1950s
Robin Smith was an England batsman of the 1990s

explanation.surface: Two former England cricketers are named, with one said to open the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the opener' looks like a cricketing opening batsman but is the definition: someone who opens locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fits and picks locks is the one called to open a jammed door.

clue.text: Powerful header struck in knockout fixture, a beauty

indicators.note: struck means struck out, removed

parts.note: a cup tie is a knockout match in a football cup competition

indicators.note: header means the first letter of the word powerful

explanation.surface: A powerful header scores in a cup match, and it is a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerful header' sounds like football, but it means the letter P, struck out of CUP TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive person, a looker.

clue.text: Low as the sky, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the colour of a clear sky is an example of this colour

explanation.surface: Someone feels down, as glum as a grey day.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low means sad, and a clear daytime sky is azure-coloured.

clue.text: 19's night air

parts.note: 19 is Miller, here bandleader Glenn Miller, whose signature tune evokes a love song sung under the night sky

explanation.surface: A Miller tune evoking the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenn Miller's best-known tune is an air, a melody, named for a song sung by night.

clue.text: Giant finally becoming shorter

indicators.note: becoming shorter means losing a letter, here the last one

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: A tall man at last shrinks.
explanation.walkthrough: AT LAST loses its final T, 'shorter', and 'becoming' links. Atlas was the Titan who held up the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas was one of the Titans of Greek myth, a race of giants.

clue.text: Relations are up a tree being fed worms?

indicators.note: being up in a nest puts the word are inside it

parts.note: a bird's nest in a tree is where chicks are fed worms

explanation.surface: Family members are imagined as fledglings up a tree, beaks open for worms.
explanation.walkthrough: Relations are one's 'nearest and dearest'; the question mark flags the loose description of a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phrase 'nearest and dearest' the word means one's closest family.

clue.text: Expand range, line less fashionable, out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order, rearranged

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A shop widens its range, dropping a product line that has gone out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes IN from RANGE LINE, and 'out' rearranges the letters left over.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand is to make bigger, a direct synonym.
